chapter: New Orleans teachers and classical musicians
title: Opening and Manuel Perez as a patient, sight-reading teacher
summary: Dominique gives his name, then describes teacher Manuel Perez: strict about lessons, an accomplished reader who sight-read at the Deluxe Cafe.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Okay, Mr. Dominant, you might give your name on here again.
Alright, you want me to give my name, Bill? Daddy Dominant. Cornelius.
Can you tell me a little bit about your teacher, Manuel Perez?

I can tell you a lot about him, Bill. Manuel Perez was a very patient man giving lessons. And he's a very accomplished musician, a good musician. One man, if you didn't know all of your lessons, you missed one measure, he'd send you back home and give you the same lesson, or he wouldn't stand for your lesson. He'd tell you, he said, you're supposed to know your lesson when you get here. And I don't care whoever you put, whatever they put me, a piece of music. Mr. Perez, he'd read it first time. I see him play First Sight, Il Trivatar in the dance floor, at the Deluxe Cafe, First Sight. And I think he's one of the best colors ever.
